name: Andrographis
summary: Andrographis has moderate human evidence for reducing upper respiratory tract infection symptoms.
description: Andrographis has moderate human evidence for reducing upper respiratory tract infection symptoms.
safetyNotes: SAFETY ALERT: Medicines containing Andrographis have been associated with unpredictable anaphylaxis, including a fatal case reported in Australia in 2024. The TGA received 287 anaphylaxis reports through 31 December 2025 and removed Andrographis from eligibility for NEW Australian listed medicines on 17 September 2026; existing listed products were not automatically banned. Throat swelling, breathing difficulty or collapse after exposure require emergency care. Pregnancy, immunosuppressant and other medication cautions also apply.

contraindications: Pregnancy (animal and traditional-use evidence of uterine-stimulant/antifertility effects)
autoimmune disease or immunosuppressant therapy without clinician review (andrographis stimulates immune signaling)
anticoagulant/antiplatelet or antihypertensive therapy without monitoring
May potentiate antihypertensive and antidiabetic medications
rare reports of anaphylaxis and elevated liver enzymes at high doses.
Prior allergy or anaphylaxis to Andrographis
evidence_grade_explanation: Both evidence signals agree on moderate evidence.
evidence_rationale: Strongest recorded design is a systematic review, drawn from 2 recorded studies, 2 in people.
